input.message: Can you build me a full-body strength routine, no equipment, for twice a week?

output.reply:
Look, I built this around where you are right now. Zero equipment, hits the entire chain twice a week, and doesn't cut corners.

We open with single-leg glute bridges to wake up that right side before touching any standing work. From there, it's Bulgarian split squats, push-ups dosed off your 30-rep baseline, bodyweight single-leg RDLs, pike push-ups for vertical push volume, and shoulder-tap planks to lock down the core. Run it twice a week with at least 48 hours between sessions, and focus on moving with complete control on every single rep.

messages.text: Can you build me a full-body strength routine, no equipment, for twice a week?

paragraphs:
Look, I built this around where you are right now. Zero equipment, hits the entire chain twice a week, and doesn't cut corners.

We open with single-leg glute bridges to wake up that right side before touching any standing work. From there, it's Bulgarian split squats, push-ups dosed off your 30-rep baseline, bodyweight single-leg RDLs, pike push-ups for vertical push volume, and shoulder-tap planks to lock down the core. Run it twice a week with at least 48 hours between sessions, and focus on moving with complete control on every single rep.

messages.text: Two things - I want to permanently swap the core phase out of the full-body strength routine you just built me, going forward, my lower back doesn't handle it well, every time, not just today. And separately, can you restructure this week specifically - add a 20 minute mobility session on Saturday, just for this week.

paragraphs: Look, that core phase is out of the template for good. If your lower back gives you grief on planks every time, keeping it in is just stubborn, not smart. And I've slotted a 20-minute mobility session onto today's schedule to keep you moving clean.

input.message: That's it for today, wrap this up.
